subject: Sparrow integration: App bridge deploy plan & SDK wiring
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Evan Blake <evan@getsparrow.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sparrow integration: App bridge deploy plan & SDK wiring

Evan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our notes, I put together a concise deploy plan for the App Bridge integration so your engineers can get unblocked quickly. High-level phases below; detailed checklist attached.

Phases (recommended):
1) Sandbox wiring (week of 2025-04-06) — install SDK, validate auth flow, basic request/response.
2) Telemetry & quotas (one week after sandbox) — enable token-level metrics, verify prefix caching behavior.
3) Staged cutover (traffic ramp over 48 hours) — start at 1% then 10% then 100%; automated fallback to hosted model on errors.
4) Post-cutover stabilization (2 weeks) — monitor latency and token usage, tune batching.

Key technical notes for your eng team to start with:
- SDK module: use the installer module (redwood-bridge v0.9+) to avoid manual retry wiring.
- Auth: exchange short-lived egress token via your vault; rotate every 6h.
- Timeouts: client-side request timeout = 8s; read timeout for streaming = 90s.
- Retries: jittered exponential backoff (base=200ms, factor=2, max=5s), max 3 retries for 5xx or 429.
- Rate limits: we’ll provision a baseline quota (10 req/s) with burst allowance; we recommend client-side token bucket to smooth spikes.
- Migration: keep old endpoint (api.sparrow.internal -> api.redwood-edge) live for 72 hours with 302 redirect at request-level for any unhandled paths.

Attached: sparrow_sdk_snippet.zip (installer + minimal samples), and the quick checklist PDF inside.

Can you confirm a sandbox start date (we proposed 2025-04-06) and who will own token rotation on your side?

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
[attachment: sparrow_sdk_snippet.zip (zip)]

From: Evan Blake <evan@getsparrow.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sparrow Infra <infra@getsparrow.io>
Date: Wed, 19 Mar 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sparrow integration: App bridge deploy plan & SDK wiring

Thanks Lauren — this looks actionable and aligned with what we discussed. A couple quick questions from infra: 

1) Token rotation: we prefer to manage rotation from our Vault (Hashi) and issue short-lived tokens to apps. Is the installer happy with a rotating bearer token (we can push a new secret to the vault every 6 hours)?
2) Traffic shaping: we have an internal traffic governor and might want to apply headroom during business hours. Will the 10 req/s baseline be adjustable from Redwood Console?
3) Can we get a short example of the recommended retry wrapper so our front-end and backend SDKs implement identical logic?

Proposed schedule: sandbox week of 2025-04-06 is doable for us; target cutover window 2025-04-20 (low-traffic Monday) if the sandbox goes well.

Attaching our internal MVP requirements doc so you can map items to the checklist (sparrow_mvp_requirements.docx).

—Evan
Evan Blake
Head of Engineering, Sparrow Labs

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Mar 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sparrow integration: deploy plan — infra notes (internal)

Looping myself in for rollout ownership. I’ll own the rollback policy, autoscale knobs, and the routing policy for the staged cutover. Quick tech clarifications for the SDK team — please pass along to Sparrow infra: 

- Retry semantics: implement the following wrapper in any client that calls the generate endpoint: jittered exponential backoff with randomization in [0.5, 1.0] multiplier; initial delay 200ms; factor 2; max delay 5s; max attempts = 3. On 429, prefer fast-fail after one retry when running under burst conditions (we’ll surface 429 counters in the console).
- Timeouts: set a total request deadline on clients at 8s (this prevents stuck connections). For streaming responses, keep an idle read timeout at 90s and heartbeat pings every 30s.
- Batching: for high-throughput internal flows, we recommend batch sizes of 8 tokens per request initially; tune based on observed p50/p95 latency.
- Fallback: configure automatic fallback route to the hosted-safeguard model (redwood-small-safe) if error rate > 5% for 5m. We will coordinate the canary condition.

I’ll prepare a short snippet (JS + Go) and drop it in the shared drive by EOD.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
